title: lockrot report
description: The document `composer lockrot --format=json` prints. Objects are open: a field added later validates against this file unchanged; the number in the id changes only when a field is removed or renamed.

activity_cache_oldest_at.description: Fetch time of the oldest repository-activity answer served from lockrot's cache; null when every answer was fetched in this run.

not_from_composer_repository.description: How many of the packages checked lockrot asked no repository about: the lock entry carries no Composer notification-url — a path, vcs, artifact or inline package entry, or a package from a `type: composer` repository that advertises no notify URL. Equals the number of findings whose `from_composer_repository` is false.

counts.description: Findings per verdict, every verdict present.

abandoned.description: The abandoned count split by what the reader can do about it: `with_replacement` is how many of the `abandoned` findings carry a `replacement` that names a package, the rest name none (or free text). `total` equals counts.abandoned. Absent from documents written before 0.11.0.

priorities.description: Findings per priority, every priority present.

exposure.description: Direct requirements that pull in attributable flagged packages (see `exposure_rule`), with how many, most first, then by name: the same count S7 carries on the requirement's finding. A direct requirement appears here only when it pulls in such a package; a flagged direct requirement that pulls in none is not listed, and its own verdict is on its finding.

exposure_rule.description: The rule `exposure` and S7 attribute by: a flagged package that is not a direct requirement counts under each direct requirement it is reachable from when there is at least one and at most `max_fan_in` of them. The direct requirements are this run's: `require-dev` counts when `include_dev` is true. The value is what this run used, not a promise; a minor release may change it. Absent from documents written before 0.13.0.

max_fan_in.description: The most direct requirements a flagged transitive package may be reached from and still be attributed to each of them; above it the package is shared infrastructure and is listed under `unattributed`.

unattributed.description: Flagged transitive packages reached from more than `exposure_rule.max_fan_in` direct requirements, in report order: counted under no entry of `exposure` and in no S7. A flagged package no direct requirement reaches (an empty `chain`, as in a lock-only run) is in neither list. Absent from documents written before 0.13.0.

fan_in.description: How many direct requirements of this run reach the package: the length of its finding's `direct_dependents`, `require-dev` included when `include_dev` is true.

libyears.description: How far behind the lock is, in libyears: for each measured finding, the years (365.25 days) between the installed version's release and the package's newest stable release, never below zero, summed. Derived from `findings`: `total` is the sum of the unrounded per-finding values (so the sum of the printed two-decimal values agrees with it to within 0.005 per measured finding), `direct_requirements` the same over `direct: true`, `measured` the number of findings whose `libyears` is not null, `unmeasured` the null ones by reason, `furthest_behind` the greatest above zero (ties to the first package name; null when nothing was measured or nothing is behind). Every drift counts, healthy patches included: this is not a measure of rot or of security, and not php-libyear's number, which sums composer.json's direct requirements (require and require-dev) and scores an undated package as zero. Absent from documents written before 0.11.0.

total.description: Sum over every measured finding, two decimals; null when `measured` is 0, since a run that could measure nothing has no sum — 0 is the answer of a run that measured packages and found none behind.

direct_requirements.description: Sum over the measured findings with `direct: true`, two decimals: the nearest number to php-libyear's. Null on the same terms as `total`.

measured.description: Findings whose `libyears` is not null. `measured` plus every value in `unmeasured` is the number of findings.

unmeasured.description: Findings with `libyears: null`, by the first reason that applies. Every non-null `libyears_unmeasured` on a finding is one of these keys, and each count is the number of findings carrying it. A later minor release may add a key, always written from then on but never added to `required`, since 0.13 documents would then fail. These keys are not a pattern plus x-known-values set: `required` lists the ones this release writes.

branch_snapshot.description: A dev pin (`dev-main`, `2.x-dev`): a commit date, not a release date.

no_stable_release_date.description: No date to trust for one end: no stable release; the newest one undated with nothing dated above the installed version (when something dated is, its date is used and the value is a lower bound); the installed version dated only by a commit its tags share and not by its monorepo parent either (where the parent lists the version, its date is the installed version's); or the lock entry without a `time`.

not_from_composer_repository.description: No metadata was asked for: the lock entry carries no Composer notification-url — a path, vcs, artifact or inline package entry, or a package from a `type: composer` repository that advertises no notify URL.

metadata_unavailable.description: Metadata was asked for and did not come: not listed, offline, budget, transport.

furthest_behind.description: The measured finding furthest behind, ties to the first package name; null when nothing was measured or nothing measured is behind.

baseline.description: How the run compared with the baseline file, null when none was used.

findings.description: One per analysed package, in report order: priority, then verdict severity, direct before transitive, then name.

version.description: The lockrot release that wrote the document.

schema.description: The document schema number this file describes.

signalId.description: A signal identifier: `S` and a number for lockrot's own, as `docs/verdicts.md` lists them, or `<vendor>:<name>` for one that does not come from lockrot. An open set: a later release under this schema number can add an id, so read one you do not know as "other". `x-known-values` lists the ids this release writes; read it as the enum to hold a document to them.

datedBy.description: The monorepo the dates were read from through its `replace` list (a package split out of laravel/framework or symfony/symfony), null when they are the package's own.

stale.description: Baselined package names absent from the analysed lock.

dev.description: Listed under packages-dev in the lock.

from_composer_repository.description: True when the lock entry carries a Composer `notification-url`. Composer writes one only for a package served by a `type: composer` repository that advertises a notify URL (`notify-batch` or `notify` in its packages.json); packagist.org and Private Packagist do. lockrot asks a repository for metadata, advisories and repository activity only about such an entry. False otherwise: a `path`, `vcs`, `artifact` or inline `package` repository entry, and also a package from a `type: composer` repository that advertises no notify URL (asset-packagist.org; a Satis build without `notify-batch`). lockrot asked no repository about a false entry, so the finding has no metadata, advisories, activity or libyears. True does not mean packagist.org. Stays a boolean for 1.x: a finer account of where an entry came from would be a separate optional open-set field, never a new type for this key. Same value as the `--explain` document's `lock.from_composer_repository`. Absent from documents written before 0.13.0; from 0.13.0 on every finding carries it.

replacement.description: On an abandoned finding, the package its repository names as the replacement, when that is a Composer package name (Packagist's field is free text; `Symfony` or a sentence stays in the evidence and is null here). Null on every other finding. Absent from documents written before 0.11.0.

chain.description: From the direct requirement down to this package; one element when it is direct. Empty when no direct requirement reaches the package: a run over a composer.lock with no composer.json beside it has no direct requirements at all, and a lock can hold a package only the skipped require-dev asks for.

libyears.description: Years (365.25 days) between the installed version's release and the package's newest stable release — or, when that release carries no date lockrot trusts, the newest trusted date of a release above the installed version, a lower bound — at least 0, two decimals. Null when not measured; from 0.13.0 on, `libyears_unmeasured` says why. Absent from documents written before 0.11.0.

libyears_unmeasured.description: Why `libyears` is null: the key of the report's `libyears.unmeasured` this finding is counted under. The reason is the first that applies, in this order: 1. not_from_composer_repository (no metadata was asked for: exactly the findings whose `from_composer_repository` is false, the lock entry carrying no Composer notification-url); 2. metadata_unavailable (asked for and did not come); 3. branch_snapshot (the installed version is a branch); 4. no_stable_release_date (no date lockrot trusts for one of the two ends; the code does not say which). The order of `x-known-values` is the block's key order, not this precedence. Null exactly where `libyears` is a number, 0 included. Counting findings by this value gives `libyears.unmeasured` key for key. An open set: a later minor release may add a reason, or split one into narrower ones, which moves findings out of the old code. Read a value you do not know as another reason the package was not measured. Optional: documents written before 0.13.0 do not carry it; from 0.13.0 on every finding does, as a string or null.

anyOf.description: A signal whose id this schema does not list, from a later release or not from lockrot: its data is any object. Every id the schema lists is typed by its own branch above and cannot take this one.

s5.description: Written for an older PHP major and released before the target's major existed, with a php constraint that admits the target only because it has no upper bound.

target_major.description: The first release of the target's major, `8.0` for a target of `8.4`; its GA is the date the release is held against. Optional: documents written before 0.11.0 do not carry it.

ga_date.description: GA of target_major. Documents written before 0.11.0 carry the target minor's GA here instead, and no target_major.

written_for_php.description: The PHP major of the constraint's lower bound, null when it has none (`*`). Optional: documents written before 0.11.0 do not carry it.

s6.description: Pinned to a branch snapshot, or no tagged release.

reason.description: Which of S6's two cases fired. `branch_snapshot`: the installed version is a branch (`dev-main`, `2.x-dev`); it is checked first, so a snapshot of a package that never released is `branch_snapshot` with has_stable_release false. `no_stable_release`: the installed version is not a branch and the repository lists no tagged version. An open set: read a value you do not know as another reason S6 fired. Optional: documents written before 0.13.0 do not carry it.

has_stable_release.description: Whether the repository lists any tagged version (a pre-release counts, a branch does not), as the explanation's metadata.has_stable_release. Null, not false, when lockrot loaded no repository metadata for the package, for example a `vcs` or `path` entry, a package the repository does not list, or metadata that did not load (the report's notes say which); null only ever comes with reason branch_snapshot. Optional: documents written before 0.13.0 do not carry it.

last_stable_release.description: The newest dated tagged release, as the explanation's metadata.last_stable_release: not necessarily the highest tag. Null when there is no tagged release, when no repository metadata was loaded, and when the highest tag carries no date lockrot trusts (undated, or on a commit other tags share) and no monorepo parent dates it; last_stable_dated_by names such a parent. Optional: documents written before 0.13.0 do not carry it.

last_stable_version.description: The version last_stable_release dates; null exactly when it is. Optional: documents written before 0.13.0 do not carry it.

last_stable_dated_by.description: The monorepo parent whose tag dates last_stable_release, null when the date is the package's own or there is none. Optional: documents written before 0.13.0 do not carry it.

snapshot_time.description: For reason branch_snapshot, the lock's `time`: the date of the commit the branch pointed at, not a release. Null for reason no_stable_release, and when the lock entry carries no time. Optional: documents written before 0.13.0 do not carry it.

s7.description: A direct requirement pulling in flagged transitive packages.

s8.description: The installed release branch stopped while a higher one kept releasing.

newest_php.description: The php requirement of the newest branch's release as the repository lists it, null when it requires no PHP. Optional: documents written before 0.11.0 do not carry it.

newest_within_reach.description: Whether the project can move onto the newest branch: its php requirement admits the project's own require.php and the target PHP. Optional: documents written before 0.11.0 do not carry it.

floor_php.description: What holds the newest branch back when it is out of reach: the project's require.php as written, or the target PHP minor; null when within reach. Optional: documents written before 0.11.0 do not carry it.

floor_source.description: Which floor floor_php is; null when the newest branch is within reach. An open set: a later release can add a floor, so read a value you do not know as "other". Optional: documents written before 0.11.0 do not carry it.

reachable_branch.description: The newest releasing higher branch within reach, the one suggested_constraint follows; the newest branch itself when that is within reach, null when none is. Optional: documents written before 0.11.0 do not carry it.

reachable_version.description: Optional: documents written before 0.11.0 do not carry it.

reachable_release.description: Optional: documents written before 0.11.0 do not carry it.

suggested_constraint.description: A caret constraint that follows the newest releasing branch within reach, null when there is none or Composer cannot suggest one.

s10.description: A check the verdict rests on did not run. Informational: it never decides a verdict, and it is carried only where the missing check could have changed one — not on a package the repository already marks abandoned, nor on an allowlisted one.

unchecked.description: One entry per check that did not run.

check.description: `repository_activity` is the forge round behind S3 and S4; `release_dates` is the package's own age, which the repository dates only by a commit its tags share. An open set: a later release can add a check, so read one you do not know as "other".

reason.description: Why it did not run. An open set: a later release can add a reason, so read one you do not know as "other".

blocks.description: The signals that could not be read without it.
Every signal the missing checks blocked, flattened.

s9.description: Security advisories on the installed version.

fixed_by.description: The lowest listed release the advisory does not affect, null when none.

fixed_on_branch.description: Whether fixed_by is on the installed release branch.

run.description: What the run was told to do. Every verdict depends on it: the thresholds decide stale from silent, the target PHP decides whether a release predates it. Optional, because reports written before 0.10.0 do not carry it.

project.description: What the report calls this project: composer.json's own `name`, or whatever `extra.lockrot.project` says instead. A display name, not an identifier — a package inside a monorepo or a private project is routinely called something that is not a vendor/name. Null where the manifest has no name and the config says nothing.

root_package.description: What Composer calls this project: the `name` of the manifest Composer reads (composer.json, or the file `COMPOSER` names), exactly as written, whatever `extra.lockrot.project` says. `project` is what the report calls the project; this is the root package's own name. Not checked against the vendor/name form. Null where the manifest has no `name` (absent, empty or not a string), or where no composer.json was read (a lock-only run). One of the two keys in `run` a document may omit, with `project_php`: reports written before 0.13.0 do not carry it; from 0.13.0 on it is always written.

target_php.description: The PHP version the project targets, as --target-php, config.platform.php or the running PHP gave it.

project_php.description: The project's own `require.php`, exactly as the manifest Composer reads writes it (composer.json, or the file `COMPOSER` names): a constraint such as `>=8.2` or `^7.4 || ^8.0`, not a version, neither normalised nor checked. The second PHP floor, beside `target_php`, that left-behind (S8) holds a higher branch against, by the lowest PHP it promises. The same value `--explain` writes as `project_php`. Null where the manifest has no `require.php` (absent, empty or not a string), or where no composer.json was read (a lock-only run). Optional: reports written before 0.13.0 do not carry it; from 0.13.0 on it is always written.

lock_file.description: The name of the lock the report describes, never its path: a published report must not carry the directory it ran in.

fail_on.description: The verdict or priority at which the run exits 1, or "none".

thresholds.description: The ages, in years, that separate one verdict from the next.

flagged_verdicts.description: The verdicts this run counted as findings, biggest first. Not a setting but the vocabulary used, so a reader need not know the severity ladder by heart.

baselineStanding.description: Where one finding stands against the baseline, null when the run read none or the baseline says nothing about this package.
